title: Residue field extensions of an etale algebra are finite separable
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$ (the preimage of $\mathfrak q$ in $A$). Then the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ (the fraction field of $B/\mathfrak q$) is a finite separable extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ via the induced map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; in particular every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a root of a separable polynomial with coefficients in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field) applied to the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, which is etale over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (base change, Algebra Tag 00U2 (4)) and has $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ as a localization at a prime, hence as a factor; equivalently Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) (2); quoted in etale-cohomology.tex Remark Tag 04HT and in the proof of Lemma Tag 04HX
